newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Albania president calls parliament for Wednesday.
newsitem.headline: Albania president calls parliament for Wednesday.

text.p: Albania's President Sali Berisha on Monday issued a decree convening the first session of the new parliament for Wednesday, the presidency said.
Berisha has repeatedly said he will resign once the new parliament is in place but the statement gave no indication of when he planned to step down.
On Sunday, Berisha's Socialist opponents, who won a big majority in the June 29 elections, said they would convene parliament themselves if Berisha failed to issue the decree.

Berisha's Democratic Party said earlier on Monday it would boycott the first session of parliament to protest at the conduct of the polls, in which the Socialists and their coalition allies won a total of 117 seats to the Democrats' 27.

Berisha says he has no wish to cohabit with a Socialist government and will resign once he has "fulfilled his constitutional obligations". His resignation is sought by the leftist alliance which fears he will try to influence the formation of the new cabinet.
Much of the country is still ruled by armed gangs and most Albanians are eager to see a new government take charge and start restoring law and order.
